messages:
nina: Hey team, quick blocker on docs PR #512. The JS streaming + function-calling example in the API guide implies the server will deliver the final function_call payload even if the stream errors mid-way. Runtime folks: is that true today?

leo: @nina can you paste the exact snippet so we can align wording? reviewers flagged it as potentially misleading.

nina: sure — here's the minimal example I used: 
```js
const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-gen-1', messages, functions: [helpFn], stream: true });
for await (const part of stream) {
  if (part.function_call) {
    // call local helper
  }
}
```

nina: reviewers want a clear statement: if the runtime fails after emitting partial chunks, will it (A) send an error-only final chunk and close, or (B) transparently fall back and provide the full function_call result?

meera: product: docs should be explicit. customers rely on the migration guide for edge changes. recommend we document current behavior and an example of a defensive client-side fallback.

runtime-bot: Current runtime behavior: it does NOT perform a server-side switch to a sync response after a streaming failure. The stream will emit an error frame and close. Server-side fallback is planned but not in prod.

leo: thanks. can you provide the exact error structure so we can show how to detect it? e.g., is it an error chunk with code, message, and a transient flag? also what HTTP status is returned?

runtime-bot: Confirmed: final stream chunk follows our streaming error schema: {"type":"error","code":"internal","message":"runtime: GPU OOM","details":{"transient":true}} then connection closes and the HTTP response is 500. We'll link the protocol doc in the PR.

nina: great — i'll update the API guide to add a short note and a tiny defensive pattern. Proposed add: try/catch around the stream loop and retry the request non-streaming once if the error.payload.details.transient is true.

leo: sounds good. keep the inline snippet minimal to avoid the docs renderer flake we've been tripping over. Move a longer example to a gist and embed a one-line sample in the doc.

ci-bot: heads up — docs preview has flaked on streaming code fences before. If you shorten the fenced block it should reduce the chance of renderer crash.

nina: i'll do that. Plan: (1) update snippet to be defensive and minimal, (2) add explicit sentence: "Runtime closes streams with an error frame on transient failures; clients should implement retry/fallback; server-side automatic fallback is planned but not available in prod.", (3) link to protocol doc for error shape, (4) reference the migration note for customers who relied on implicit fallback.

meera: product wants a small roadmap callout saying "server-side fallback planned (target: upcoming quarter)" so customers aren't surprised.

leo: once you push, @docs-bot please rerun preview. If preview passes we'll remove the draft label and request final reviewers.

nina: pushing now. cc @docs-bot

docs-bot: received push to docs/pr-512 — queued preview job id 101007.

docs-bot: preview job 101007 completed — renderer succeeded. link: https://ci.redwood/preview/101007 (status: success).

nina: thanks all. marking thread resolved for reviewer blockers. i'll @reviewers when PR is out of draft.

leo: nice and quick. also add a one-line note in the migration guide and SDK-compat doc. reviewers will look there first.

nina: added both as follow-up commit. closing this blocker.
